newsitem.title: FRANCE: Carlos the Jackal's suit against publisher set.
newsitem.headline: Carlos the Jackal's suit against publisher set.

text.p: Guerrilla mastermind "Carlos the Jackal" will go to court on February 26 in a bid to win damages of $170,000 over a book he says has undermined his chances of a fair trial, legal sources said on Thursday.

Carlos, whose real name is Illich Ramirez Sanchez and who was spirited out of Sudan to France in 1994, is in a Paris prison awaiting trial for guerrilla actions in the 1970s and 1980s which French authorities say caused 83 deaths in Europe and the Middle East.

HIs lawyers argue that the book "Carlos: The Secret Networks of International Terrorism", by journalist Bernard Violet, published by Seuil, blames him for a string of bombings and assassinations in France, violating his right to be considered innocent until proved guilty.
The Venezuelan-born ultra-leftist lost an earlier bid to have the book banned in October on the grounds that it breached French privacy laws.

Hia written complaint, in which he lists his occupation as "professional revolutionary", says Violet's book illegally included confidential reports from the investigation, including French and former East German secret service documents.
He has already been convicted in his absence by a French court and sentenced to life in prison for the 1975 killings of two secret service agents.
He is also being investigated over a total of six bombings and killings in France. Carlos's boldest attack was the 1975 kidnapping of 11 OPEC oil ministers attending a conference in Vienna.
